one_line: An educational video analyzing the psychological and social effects of disclosing cosmetic surgery using scientific studies and celebrity examples.

hook.what_happens: A before-and-after comparison of Bella Hadid with the question: 'Should you lie about getting work done?'
hook.why_it_works: It poses a controversial question about a highly recognizable celebrity, immediately engaging the viewer's curiosity.

onscreen_text.text: Should you lie about getting work done?
Jaeger, B., Bucker, B., van der Meulen, J., & van Vugt, M. (2025). Face value: The effect of facial aesthetic treatment on first impressions and partner preferences. Perception, 54(9), 651-673.

Liang, F., Zhu, M., Lei, Y., Zhang, S., Liang, M., Tao, Z., ... & He, X. (2023). Untrustworthy beauty: Beautification strategies cause female applicators to be perceived untrustworthy. Psychology of Aesthetics, Creativity, and the Arts.

transcript.text: If you get work done and it makes you more attractive, but then you go on and you talk about it, will it actually make you less dateable?
When people evaluate the face itself, sort of cosmetic work does not seem to hurt and may even slightly improve first impressions.

Jaeger and colleagues found that women who had minimally invasive treatments were judged somewhat more attractive and more desirable for short term dating, although the effect was relatively small and they didn't extend to long term desirability.
However, the picture changes once cosmetic work is disclosed.
Several studies have found that women who seek or undergo cosmetic procedures can be judged less favorably on traits such as trustworthiness, warmth and authenticity.
The face itself has not changed, only the observer's knowledge of it has.
This suggests men may be evaluating two things at once: the face, and what cosmetic work is perceived to say about the person itself.
If the work is subtle and not disclosed, men respond primarily to the visible result, which appears neutral to slightly positive.
But once it becomes known, some men attach negative social meanings to that partially, which offsets the visual benefit.
So, want us to analyze your face? Click the link in bio at qoves.com.

narrative_arc: Introduce the core question: does disclosing cosmetic work reduce attractiveness?
Present evidence showing cosmetic work itself slightly improves first impressions.
Introduce the 'Disclosure Effect' where revealing work lowers perceived warmth and trustworthiness.
Explain the dual evaluation theory (evaluating both the face and the social meaning of surgery).
Demonstrate how disclosure offsets the visual benefits of subtle work.
Call to action for personal facial analysis.

cta.what: Get your facial analysis at qoves.com

what_makes_it_work: Uses peer-reviewed scientific citations to back up claims, elevating it above standard gossip content.
Maintains a clean, minimalist aesthetic with a consistent pastel blue color palette.
Leverages highly recognizable celebrities to illustrate abstract psychological concepts.

animations.name: Grid Scan Overlay
animations.what_moves: A dotted grid overlay sweeps across the face image.
animations.purpose: Simulates a digital facial analysis scan.
animations.reusable_as: Scanning or analyzing any portrait or product image.
animations.would_need_building: A grid texture mask that sweeps horizontally across a target layer.

animations.name: Chat Bubble Pop
animations.what_moves: A text message bubble scales up from the side of the face.
animations.purpose: Represents a quote or internal thought about cosmetic work.
animations.reusable_as: Displaying user testimonials or conversational text.

animations.name: Face Scanner Box
animations.what_moves: A bounding box with 'EVALUATING...' text sweeps down the face.
animations.purpose: Indicates an automated aesthetic evaluation process.
animations.reusable_as: Highlighting specific regions of interest in an image.
animations.would_need_building: A bounding box overlay with a vertical scanning line and status text.

animations.name: Bar Chart Growth
animations.what_moves: Vertical bars grow upwards; emoji icons pop in above them.
animations.purpose: Presents scientific data comparing treated vs natural faces.
animations.would_need_building: An animated bar chart component where bars scale vertically and labels fade in.

animations.name: Celebrity Montage
animations.what_moves: A rapid sequence of celebrity portrait clips replacing each other.
animations.purpose: Shows examples of public figures who disclosed cosmetic work.
animations.reusable_as: Quickly showcasing a gallery of examples or case studies.

animations.name: Flowchart Arrow Draw
animations.what_moves: Downward arrows draw on, and text blocks slide down in columns.
animations.purpose: Illustrates the negative impact of disclosing cosmetic procedures.
animations.reusable_as: Showing cause-and-effect relationships or step-by-step flows.
animations.would_need_building: A flowchart component with animated directional arrows and staggered text blocks.

animations.name: Split Face Comparison
animations.what_moves: Two labeled versions of the same face slide slightly apart.
animations.purpose: Compares the perception of 'natural' vs 'enhanced' versions of a face.
animations.would_need_building: A dual-panel split comparison component that slides outward from a central seam.

animations.name: Step Number Pop
animations.what_moves: Numbered circular badges pop in sequentially.
animations.reusable_as: Listing steps, phases, or key points in a sequence.

animations.name: Slider Rating Pointer
animations.what_moves: A pointer moves along a horizontal scale, changing the numeric value.
animations.purpose: Quantifies the shift in social perception.
animations.reusable_as: Showing ratings, scores, or adjustments on a scale.
animations.would_need_building: A horizontal slider scale with an animated indicator and dynamic value display.

animation_language_summary.how_things_enter: Elements scale up with elastic spring physics or slide in from the sides.
animation_language_summary.how_things_leave: Elements fade out or are replaced abruptly by the next scene.
animation_language_summary.how_scenes_change: Hard cuts with occasional slide-overs or full-screen color wipes.
animation_language_summary.what_stays_still: The muted blue-grey background and top-level question text.
animation_language_summary.rhythm: Highly dynamic, alternating between static data presentation and rapid visual demonstrations.
